title: The address in his pocket

text.text: At the bend in the path Amaro could still see his mother's house. He had saved for his own fare. The street in Quarry Bend was only four words on a slip of paper, and he ran his finger over them once more before putting it away.
Twelve days later he followed the mill whistle up from the pier. At number fourteen Manuel had left the door on the latch.

title: Thread in the window

text.text: Rosa held the small sleeve against the daylight and picked out a loose thread. Across the roofs a mill whistle told her Amaro would be home before supper. Their daughter Helena was already asleep, with both fists closed.
Rosa set the finished sleeve across the back of a chair. When the baby woke, she took her to the window to watch for Amaro.

title: The lantern at number fourteen

text.text: When the fog rolled up Rope Walk Street, the houses looked alike from the pier. Rosa put a lantern on the table while Amaro went to meet Manuel. Four years earlier a scrap of paper had been enough to get Amaro to that door.
When the men came in, Rosa turned the lantern down. The kettle had only just begun to sing.

ask.text: Where would you leave a light for someone coming home after dark?

more.text: - Our version: the whole lantern scene is invented. The address is the one on the demo ship's list.
